title: Prefetch Latency Signatures and SDK Handoff Heuristics (PRD Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working PRD for an experimentation sprint that explores: 1) measuring 'prefetch latency signatures' — a compact set of runtime signals that explain when speculative prefetching helps or hurts user-perceived latency/cost; 2) defining SDK handoff heuristics so client integrations can safely request progressive outputs, tool calls, and lightweight checkpoints; and 3) a telemetry surface that ties quality regressions to prefetch decisions.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Customers want low tail latency for interactive experiences using hosted streaming (chat, code, search).
- Aggressive prefetching (e.g., speculative model token generation, warming tool calls) can reduce median latency but increases cost and sometimes harms correctness when model outputs diverge from the final context.
- Current SDKs provide primitive streaming hooks but no standardized handoff semantics or telemetry to reason about prefetch tradeoffs.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Define a minimal "prefetch signature" (<= 6 signals) that correlates with 95th percentile latency reductions >= 20% for target workloads without more than 5% increase in token cost per session.
- Ship an SDK-level handoff API (JS + Python) that surfaces: prefetch intent, provisional output, checkpoint tokens, and an idempotent tool-call token.
- Produce a telemetry dashboard (Console) that maps prefetch decisions to latency/cost/quality metrics and surfaces false-prefetch rate.
- Create a rollout plan with canary and kill-switch primitives for auto-fallback to non-prefetching flows.

User stories / personas:
- Product engineer (chat): "I want provisional suggestions to show in the UI while final content completes, without committing to tool executions prematurely."
- Platform SRE: "I need a kill switch that removes prefetching at a tenant level when errors spike or cost budgets are exceeded."
- Solutions engineer: "I want to be able to recommend SDK knobs to customers and reason about effect on latency/cost in their workload."

Proposed API surfaces (high-level):
- Server-side /hosted-api options: prefetch_mode: [off, conservative, aggressive], prefetch_budget: integer (max speculative tokens), prefetch_scope: [prefix-only, tool-primed, full-seq].
- Streaming frames: introduce 'provisional' frame attribute with stable frame_id and provisional=true | committed=true flags. Frames can be annotated with tool_tokens: [idempotent-token].
- SDK helper: sdk.prefetch.start(intent, expected_tool_calls, deadline_ms) -> returns PreFetchHandle with methods: onProvisional(frame_cb), commit(), abort(), metrics()

SDK ergonomics notes (JS + Python patterns):
- Lightweight defaults: conservative prefetch enabled by default for 'interactive' SDK builder with small prefetch_budget (8 tokens) and 100ms speculative timeout.
- Declarative fallbacks: provide composition helpers that allow apps to present provisional UI states and resolve automatically on commit/abort.
- Idempotent tool-calls: SDK will issue tool-call tokens only at commit() unless explicit 'tool-warm' flag is used by app with audit logging.
- Backpressure: SDK exposes a per-session prefetch_budget_meter and emits events when usage crosses 70% to encourage application-level flow control.

Prefetch Latency Signature (candidate signals):
1) client_network_rtt_ms (p50/p95)
2) backend_inflight_batches (count)
3) prefix_entropy_estimate (model-derived score for how deterministic the prefix is)
4) predicted_time_to_first_token_ms (model+routing estimate)
5) stable_prefix_probability (likelihood that additional tokens will not change tool-call decisions)
6) recent_false_prefetch_rate (rate of aborted speculative commits in past N minutes)

Telemetry / observability schema (Console):
- At request-level: prefetch_mode, prefetch_budget, provisional_frames_count, commit_latency_ms, abort_reason, token_delta_cost.
- Aggregates: false_prefetch_rate, avg_saved_latency_by_mode, cost_delta_by_mode, quality_regression_by_prompt_set.
- Alerts: alert when false_prefetch_rate > 8% for 10m or when cost_delta_by_mode > 15% month-over-month.

Quality and safety considerations:
- Conservatively we forbid prefetch-driven tool commits for high-impact tool families (payments, code-deploy, delete operations). Tools may be 'warmable' only for read-only or sandboxed variants.
- All speculative actions must be scoped to be reversible or non-mutating unless the app explicitly requests commit with stronger auth.
- Provide a 'sandbox' tool flag that allows speculative outputs to call a sandboxed version of the tool for preview.

Metrics / success criteria (initial experiment):
- Deploy to 10% of interactive free-tier tenants for 2 weeks.
- Target: 15–30% median latency improvement on target prompt set, < 7% increase in per-session tokens, false_prefetch_rate < 6%, and no customer-facing correctness incidents.

Rollout plan and safety knobs:
- Phase 0: internal dogfood experiments + lab harness across 5 representative apps (conversational help, code assist, search summarization).
- Phase 1: 10% canary on live traffic with kill-switch and tenant-level opt-out.
- Phase 2: 50% selective rollout, add model-bound heuristics (only on models with stable_prefix_probability > 0.7).
- Fail fast conditions: spike in tool errors, false_prefetch_rate > threshold, or drift in quality metrics.

Implementation notes for the serving runtime team (observations):
- Need lightweight hints from runtime: predicted_time_to_first_token_ms and model-stability signals must be exposed from compilation/kernels.
- Prefix entropy_estimate requires a small scoring endpoint in model runner — add as a sampled metric to avoid perf regressions.
- KV cache warm-up may be useful: attaching a 'cache_preload' hint to speculative requests.

Open questions and tradeoffs (non-exhaustive):
- How to balance developer ergonomics (easy provisional UI) vs. cost accountability (who pays for speculative tokens)? Suggested default: platform covers a tiny prefetch_budget for free-tier; paid tiers allow larger budgets.
- How do we version provisional frame semantics across SDKs and server running older agents? Need backward-compat handshake.
- What constitutes an acceptable false_prefetch? Is 5% too high for high-safety apps? We should add per-tenant adjustable thresholds.

Experimentation plan / tasks (next 6 sprints):
- Sprint 1: prototype SDK prefetch handle (JS) + basic server prefetch_mode flag. Create lab harness and testbed prompts.
- Sprint 2: integrate signature signals telemetry into request logs + Console chart.
- Sprint 3: idempotent tool token flow + sandbox tool runner.
- Sprint 4: broaden canary, capture quality regressions, refine heuristics.

Appendix: Quick dev notes and example usage (JS pseudo):
const pre = sdk.prefetch.start({intent: 'assist', expected_tool_calls: ['search'], deadline_ms: 200});
pre.onProvisional(frame => showProvisionalUI(frame.content));
// when user accepts or model stabilizes
await pre.commit(); // commit sends final model stream and executes idempotent tool tokens
// else
pre.abort('user-cancelled');

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a thought-through draft, intentionally pragmatic and conservative. Looking for engineering estimates on: (A) model runner work to compute prefix stabilities (B) storage/trace volume impact of provisional frames (C) SDK ergonomics feedback from mobile and React Native teams.

Proposed reviewers: product-hosted-api leads, eng-serving-runtime, devexp SDK owners, observability PM.
